questions.question: What is the difference between a non-living thing and a thing that was once living?
questions.expected_answer: A non-living thing, such as sand, rock or plastic, was never alive. A once-living thing, such as a shell, driftwood or a feather, came from a living thing but is now dead. Neither can carry out the seven life processes now.

questions.question: Why is fire not a living thing even though it seems to grow and move?
questions.expected_answer: To be living, a thing must carry out all seven life processes. Fire may seem to grow and move and use wood, but it cannot carry out all of them, for example it does not sense or reproduce like a living thing, so it is not alive.

questions.question: Name three things we use every day that were once living, and say what living thing each came from.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: a wooden desk or paper from a tree, a cotton T-shirt from the cotton plant, a leather shoe from the skin of a cow, a wool jersey from a sheep, coal from ancient plants.
